text:
dave (customer): Hey team, hitting 401s in prod only after bundling with Vite. Local/unbundled works fine. Using @redwood/inference-node v2.2.0, Node 18. Repro steps below.

dave (customer): Repro steps:
1) npm i @redwood/inference-node@2.2.0
2) import client from 'redwood-inference'
3) build with Vite (SSR), deploy bundle
4) Requests to /v1/generate return 401 Unauthorized only in bundled app

dave (customer): Minimal call:
```js
import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'
const c = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
await c.generate({ model: 'redwood-medium', prompt: 'hi' })
```

dave (customer): Logs from prod bundle (obf):
```
[ERROR] request to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate failed, status 401
headers: {host: 'api.redwood.ai', 'content-type': 'application/json'}
```

alice (support): Sorry you're hitting this, @dave. Quick q: can you confirm the Authorization header is present in your production requests? Also which bundler plugin are you using to replace env vars? :eyes:

dave (customer): Good call. I pulled the outgoing request headers in prod and Authorization is missing. Locally (dev server) it is present. Using Vite with @rollup/plugin-replace to inline env vars.

bob (devex): Common pattern: bundlers sometimes resolve conditional-exports to the browser entry which expects the key to be injected differently or relies on global fetch wrapper that doesn't attach headers. Can you paste your package.json exports for the SDK?

dave (customer): Exports from node_modules/@redwood/inference/package.json:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  },
  "./node": "./dist/node.js"
}
```

dave (customer): Workaround: importing from 'redwood-inference/node' seems to make the header appear again in prod. But that's not ideal for our codebase.

alice (support): That suggests Vite might be resolving to the wrong entry (import -> mjs browserish build) which doesn't wire up the env->header creation for server runtimes. Can you try forcing the Node entry with: import Redwood from 'redwood-inference/node' and confirm? Also please try disabling env inlining to see if process.env is available at runtime.

dave (customer): Tried import from /node and it fixed it. Authorization header present and 200s now. But this breaks portability between serverless and edge envs.

carol (eng): Thanks for the debug. We shipped a browser-optimized ESM build that assumes a different auth flow (browser key input), so bundlers that pick that build for SSR will omit the server auth shim. We'll investigate conditional exports mapping to make node/server entry higher priority for server-side bundlers. In the short term: 1) import from 'redwood-inference/node' 2) or pin the CJS entry (require) 3) upgrade to v2.3.1 when released — includes a fix for resolving when bundlers pick browser entry. cc @deploy-bot for release notes.

deploy-bot: Added task RD-INF-412 to backlog: "Ensure SDK conditional exports prefer node entry for SSR bundlers". ETA next patch release.

bob (devex): Another quick workaround: in Vite config add:
```js
resolve: { alias: { 'redwood-inference': 'redwood-inference/dist/node.js' } }
```
or force ssr: { noExternal: ['redwood-inference'] } so Rollup doesn't rewrite exports.

dave (customer): Thanks all — import from /node + Vite alias both worked. We'll hold on upgrade until patch is out. Appreciate the quick help :tada:

alice (support): Glad it's working — marking this thread resolved. If you can share a minimal repro repo (private), we can attach to RD-INF-412 to validate the fix before release.
